Home Dumbbell Back Day

Master complete back development at home by adjusting your grip angle and elbow positioning across 5 targeted dumbbell row and fly variations.

15–20 min

Exercise Flow

Check off each exercise as you complete sets. Rest timer at the bottom.
01

Underhand Dumbbell Row (Lat Focus)

3 × 10–12 reps
Latissimus DorsiBicepsLower Back
  • Hold dumbbells with a supinated (underhand) grip
  • Pull dumbbells back toward your hips while driving elbows straight back

Why: Maximizes lower lat engagement by keeping elbows tight and pulling back towards the waist.

02

Neutral Grip Bent Over Row (Mid-Back Focus)

3 × 10–12 reps
RhomboidsMiddle TrapeziusLatissimus Dorsi
  • Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other (neutral grip)
  • Row towards lower ribcage while squeezing shoulder blades together

Why: Builds mid-back thickness by pulling toward the mid-torso with a neutral grip.

03

Pronated Bent Over Row (Teres Major Focus)

3 × 10–12 reps
Teres MajorUpper LatsRhomboids
  • Use an overhand (pronated) grip
  • Row dumbbells towards upper abdomen with elbows slightly flared

Why: Shifts emphasis to the upper lats and teres major to help widen your back.

04

Wide Elbow Row (Rear Delt & Upper Traps)

3 × 10–12 reps
Rear DeltoidsUpper TrapeziusInfraspinatus
  • Flare elbows outwards at roughly 70-90 degrees
  • Pull dumbbells towards upper chest level while keeping core engaged

Why: Isolates upper back depth and rear shoulders by widening elbow path.

05

Bent Over Reverse Fly (Trapezius Focus)

3 × 12–15 reps
TrapeziusRear DeltoidsRhomboids
  • Maintain a slight bend in elbows
  • Raise weights outward in an arc until parallel with shoulders

Why: Strengthens scapular retractors and upper trapezius muscles.

Trainer Tips

  • Hinge at your hips with a flat spine to protect your lower back throughout every rep.
  • Control the eccentric (lowering) phase of each repetition to maximize muscle tension.
